findings.claim: escalation_door's executed decision table never calls paid_path_open the way production calls it — every row and every _demo assertion passes token= explicitly, so the `token is None` branch app.py actually takes is unbound, and a three-line edit there makes an UNCONFIGURED deployment bill every anonymous request with the whole gate green.
findings.evidence: eval_adapter.py:3448-3458 (all nine rows pass token=configured) and gate.py:99 (_demo lambda likewise). app.py:251 calls gate.paid_path_open(header, ESCALATION_ENABLED) with NO token=, so gate.py's `configured_token() if token is None else …` is the only production entry and no case exercises it. With the secret UNSET and no header: shipped tree 0 outbound on all three routes; mutant gives upload outbound=1, url outbound=1, envelope reason 'the deployment is configured for the paid tier'. This is exactly the UNSET IS CLOSED property gate.py:17-23, ADR-036 §h2, README and escalation-door.json all name as the one that matters.
findings.repro: insert `if token is None: return True, …` above gate.py's token normalisation -> gate self-check exit 0 and the suite score identical to clean
findings.acceptance: The table contains at least one row calling paid_path_open(presented, armed) with NO token= keyword, under a patched env asserting False when unset and the same verdict as the explicit-token row when configured — watched red on that edit.
findings.orchestrator_verified: REPRODUCED. The mutation leaves gate.py's self-check at exit 0 and the invariant score byte-identical to the clean copy.

findings.claim: escalation_door pins the SHAPE of the door's one call site but not its ARGUMENTS, so both operands can be swapped for money-spending values while invariant and fast stay byte-identical to clean.
findings.evidence: eval_adapter.py:3523-3560 checks paid_path_open is called once inside _run, its verdict bound to a name, and that escalate=/budget=/view['escalation'] use that name — it never inspects n.args. M4: first arg becomes request.headers.get(gate.HEADER, gate.configured_token()) — with a secret configured, an anonymous request with NO header gets upload=1, url=1 and an envelope falsely reading 'a valid x-escalation-token header was presented'. M6: second arg becomes literal True — with SEC10K_ESCALATION_ENABLED=0 (the operator's runaway stop) and a valid token, shipped gives 0 outbound, M6 gives upload 1, url 1, while /api/meta still publishes escalation_enabled: false.
findings.repro: apply either edit to app.py:251-253 -> both suites identical to clean
findings.acceptance: The check asserts the first argument is a read of gate.HEADER off the request parameter and the second is the module's off-switch constant — watched red on both M4 and M6.
